messages:
anya: heads-up — thinking about adding small in-console coachmarks for 'safe rollout' when someone flips a runtime config. show the telemetry gates that will be monitored and quick links to related dashboards. quick opinions?

mike-g: big yes. we need to avoid scary UX where people click enable and nothing explains rollback criteria. coachmarks could show: sample size, expected latency delta, error-rate thresholds, and which metrics are gated. :thumbsup:

devex-liz: agreed. also suggest a compact preview of historical signals for the target cohort (like sparkline for p95/p50/errors) — helps decide canary size. we should not fetch full dashboards to avoid slow console load. lightweight aggregated query.

infra-jon: important - whatever we show has to come from the same telemetry contract used by the rollout automation. can't have two different definitions for "errors". propose an internal endpoint: GET /internal/config-rollout/preview?config_id=...&cohort=... that returns the small stats.

product-ana: can we show an "estimated impact" card that extrapolates expected token cost and latency delta for 1h/24h based on recent traffic? product will use that in docs.

anya: sketch of preview API payload i had in mind:

```
GET /internal/config-rollout/preview?config=route-by-cost-v2&cohort=20%25
200 OK
{
  "samples": 12000,
  "p50_latency_ms": 45.3,
  "p95_latency_ms": 123.6,
  "error_rate": 0.003,
  "expected_cost_delta_pct": 2.4
}
```

mike-g: looks fine. question: should the console call that endpoint directly or go through the public control-plane API? public API might have rate limits. for preview we want low-latency read path with safe auth.

infra-jon: console should call our control-plane proxy which caches preview responses for 30s and debounces requests. heavy queries should be kicked off as async and shown with a spinner. also need RBAC — not everyone should see health metrics for other teams.

devex-liz: UX note — keep wording non-technical. "Expected impact on latency" vs "p95 delta". let advanced users expand raw metrics.

anya: telemetry semantics: gating should compare current period vs baseline cohort. baseline = last 24h for the whole service, cohort = same time window for the sampled users. gating rules: p95 increase > 10% OR error_rate increase > 0.5% triggers fail. we should make these tunable per-config.

product-ana: can we show a small checkbox "Auto-pause on gate failure" in the coachmark? default on for orgs with SLAs.

mike-g: backend implication: rollout orchestration needs to subscribe to metric deltas and have a decision loop. we already have rollout-bot but it's crude. rollout-bot: @rollout-bot can you confirm current capabilities?

rollout-bot: thanks @mike-g — current bot supports: staged percentage increases, health checks based on raw traffic and 5m error rate, and immediate rollback on high-severity alerts. does NOT support custom metric deltas or cost-estimates yet.

infra-jon: so tasks: (1) spec preview API + caching (2) extend rollout-bot to accept custom gate predicates (json) and an "auto-pause" flag (3) design coachmark copy + compact viz (4) auth/role scoping. who's owning 1/2?

anya: i'll take 1 (preview API + schema) — will draft proto this week. mike-g take 2?

mike-g: i'll own rollout-bot changes. will need a small schema for predicates, e.g.

```
{
  "metric": "p95_latency",
  "comparator": ">",
  "threshold_pct": 10,
  "baseline_window_mins": 1440,
  "cohort_window_mins": 60
}
```

devex-liz: i'll do the coachmark mock and copy. infra-jon please add caching + RBAC details to the spec.

product-ana: also add an analytics event: config_rollout_preview_shown and config_rollout_enabled with attributes (cohort_pct, auto_pause). we'll use that to measure adoption.

anya: noted. one more nit: console should show a tiny explanation if the preview has low sample count (<100) and recommend bumping cohort or running a dry-run.

mike-g: re: dry-run — we should expose a dry-run toggle that executes the routing decision path but doesn't modify global state; it should run the same code path as real rollout to surface surprises. infra-jon: can we support that cheaply?

infra-jon: yes, dry-run mode can be a fan-out that forks evaluation into a limited test queue and reports metrics. cost is trackable; we should gate it behind a flag and quota to avoid abuse.

anya: perfect. i'll include dry-run endpoint in the preview API doc. timeline: initial spec PR by end of week, rollout-bot prototype next sprint.

mike-g: thanks. small follow-up — let's add a tiny telemetry KPI in the rollout dashboard for "preview vs actual" accuracy so we can tune estimation heuristics.

product-ana: love that. ok lets sync next Tues to review mocks + API proto. :calendar:

anya: thx everyone — filing ACs and will ping when PR is up.
